How to Submit Public Comment

Members of the Public who wish to submit public comment may do so using one of
the following methods. Public comment is limited to the time allotted.

In-Person: Complete a Speaker Card, indicating the agenda item number and submit
it to the City Clerk prior to the meeting. Speakers shall be limited to three (3) minutes
per person per item. At the Mayor’ s discretion, the time limit may be shortened to
allow all speakers to address the City Council.

Website: Electronic submission of Public Comment is available via the City’s website
as noted below. Public Comment submitted electronically by 4:00 P.M. on the meeting
day will be forwarded to the City Council before the meeting for their consideration,
but will not be read during the meeting. Comments submitted after 4:00 P.M. will be
forwarded to Council but may not be received before the meeting.

Please submit your comments using the online public comment form at
Public Comment.

  C. CASH AND INVESTMENT REPORT – OCTOBER 2024

  In accordance with the City of San Gabriel’s 2024-2025 Adopted Investment
  Policy (Resolution No. 24-35) and California Government Code Section 53646,
  the Finance Director is to render an investment report to the City Council, City
  Treasurer, City Manager, and the City Attorney. The Cash and Investment

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council receive and file the Cash and
  Investment Report for October 2024.

  D. APPROVAL OF A THREE-YEAR SUBSCRIPTION TO MICROSOFT OFFICE 365
  FOR ALL CITY DEPARTMENTS, EXCEPT FOR POLICE, IN AN ANNUAL
  AMOUNT OF $62,045.75

  The current license agreement for Microsoft 365, which covers a range of
  productivity tools essential for daily operations, is set to expire at the end of
  December 2024. The proposed annual cost for Microsoft 365 subscription is
  $62,045.75 per year, which includes all City Departments except Police. The
  payment is due on a year-to-year basis and the pricing is locked in for the three-
  year subscription period. Funds have been appropriated in the Fiscal Year 2024-
  2025 Information Technology Internal Service Fund for this purchase. Annually,
  an adjustment is made for the actual subscriptions utilized.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  3
   Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to enter
  into a three-year subscription agreement with Microsoft Office for Office 365,
  which includes all City Departments except for Police.

  E. RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING THE ACCEPTANCE OF A $40,000 GRANT
  FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENERGY COMMISSION FOR THE CALIFORNIA
  AUTOMATED PERMIT PROCESSING (CALAPP) PROGRAM [RESOLUTION
  NO. 24-62]

  The City of San Gabriel has been awarded a $40,000 grant from the California
  Energy Commission to implement SolarAPP+, and automated platform for
  processing residential solar permits. The funds will allow the streamlining of the
  City’s solar permitting process, in line with Senate Bill 379. If appropriated,
  funds will be allocated to the Community Development Department for use in
  implementing SolarAPP+ and integrating it with the City’s existing permitting
  software. This is a State reimbursement grant, so initial expenses will be drawn
  from the City’s General Fund, with reimbursement expected upon project
  completion.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-62 authorizing
  the City Manager, or their designee, to execute the grant agreement with the
  California Energy Commission, accept the $40,000 in California Automated
  Permit Processing Program grant funds, and amend the 2024-2025 Fiscal Year
  budget to appropriate the funds accordingly.

  F. BUDGET APPROPRIATION REQUEST FOR $40,000 IN CONTRACTUAL
  BUILDING INSPECTION SERVICES [RESOLUTION NO. 24-64]

  Due to a significant number of current development projects, as well as
  increasing community needs, the City requires additional building inspection
  services to maintain an uninterrupted level of service in the Building and Safety
  Division. In February of this year, the City executed a Professional Services
  Agreement with RKA Consulting Group and VCA Code Group. To date, contract
  Building Inspectors hired through this agreement have worked with staff and
  project teams to ensure construction projects and permits move forward while
  maintaining community safety. Should the City Council approve the
  appropriation request, funding would be allocated from the General Fund to

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  4
   the Building and Safety Division General Contractual Services Fund (121-810-
  16-22-000) in the amount of $40,000 for Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

  1. Approve Resolution No. 24-64, increasing appropriations by $40,000 in the
  general fund for the costs of contractual building inspection services.

  2. Authorize the City Manager, or designee, to execute an agreement with VCA
  Code Group and RKA Consulting Group to provide building inspection
  services.

  G. ORDINANCE NO. 714: APPROVING A GENERAL PLAN AMENDMENT,
  ZONE CHANGE, DENSITY BONUS, AND STREET VACATION FOR A ONE
  HUNDRED PERCENT AFFORDABLE SENIOR HOUSING DEVELOPMENT AT
  405 S. DEL MAR AVENUE (GPA24-001, ZC24-001) – SECOND READING
  AND ADOPTION

  Adoption of Ordinance No. 714 would amend the General Plan Land Use from
  Light Industrial to High Density Residential, Zoning from M-1 (Light
  Manufacturing) to R-3 (Multiple Family Residence), and approve a Density
  Bonus and Street Vacation for a one hundred percent affordable senior housing
  development at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue. The Fiscal Year 2023-2024 Adopted
  Budget includes the cost for required legal publication (Account No. 121-702-
  00-65-000) and codification (Account No. 121-702-00-22-000) of the
  ordinance.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This project was
  reviewed for compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA).
  This project is exempt from the requirement of CEQA, per Guideline Section
  21080.40 (Definitions; affordable housing projects and rezoning exemption).
  Technical studies, including traffic, acoustic, and a Phase I and Phase II
  environmental site assessment were prepared by the applicant team and
  submitted to the City and Department of Toxic Substances Control for review.

  On July 23, 2024, the City submitted letters, requesting tribal consultation with
  the associated tribal representatives by August 22, 2024. The City received a
  request for consultation from the Gabrielino Band of Mission Indians – Kizh

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  5
   Nation. Consultation concluded on September 3, 2024. The project site has a
  moderate sensitivity for buried Native American archaeological deposits and
  cultural materials. Therefore, the potential to tribal cultural resources on-site is
  moderate. Given the moderate sensitivity of the project site, even with the
  previous disturbance, there could still be a moderate likelihood of encountering
  tribal cultural resources during project construction. The Native American Historic
  Resource Act; Archeological, Paleontological, and Historical Sites; Native
  American Historical, Cultural, and Sacred Sites (Public Resources Code Section
  5097-5097.994) specifies the procedures to be followed in the event of the
  unexpected discovery of human remains on nonfederal public lands. Adherence
  to existing State regulations and the procedures in the City’s Historic Preservation
  and Cultural Resources Ordinance (SGMC Section 153.630); would ensure that
  potential impacts on tribal cultural resources would be reduced to less than
  significant levels.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council waive reading and adopt Ordinance No.
  714 entitled, “An Ordinance of the City Council of the City of San Gabiel,
  California, Approving a General Plan Amendment, Zone Change, Density Bonus,
  and Street Vacation for a one hundred percent affordable senior housing
  development at 405 S. Del Mar Avenue.”

  H. REQUEST FOR SECOND AMENDMENT TO PROFESSIONAL SERVICES
  AGREEMENT WITH ARCHITECTURAL RESOURCES GROUP (ARG) FOR
  PREPARATION OF HISTORIC RESOURCES SURVEY PHASE 2

  The Community Development Department is requesting a Second Amendment
  to an existing Professional Services Agreement with Architectural Resources
  Group for preparation of a citywide Historic Resources Survey Phase 2. The
  project is nearing completion, but additional time is needed for the completion
  of the Historic Resources Survey Phase 2 Report. No additional funds are
  requested as a part of this term extension. Funds have already been allocated
  as part of Fiscal Year 2024-2025.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council:

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  6
   1. Approve the Second Amendment to the Professional Services Agreement
  with Architectural Resources Group to extend the term of the agreement till
  March 3, 2025; and

  2. Authorize the City Manager to execute the amendment with Architectural
  Resources Group for preparation of a citywide Historic Resources Survey
  Phase 2.

  I. JOINT TAX TRANSFER RESOLUTION CITY OF SAN GABRIEL ANNEXATION
  5623 N. GLADYS AVENUE (ASSESSOR PARCEL NUMBER 5374-027-005)
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-65]

  Consideration of a Joint Tax Transfer Resolution accepting the negotiated
  exchange of property tax revenue resulting from the annexation of property
  located at 5623 N. Gladys Avenue from the County of Los Angeles to the City
  of San Gabriel. The City would receive the base of $1,060 in the property tax
  revenue from this property tax transfer into the City, and this base may grow
  by 2% annually (Account No. 121-3111).

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: The proposed Joint
  Tax Transfer would be exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act
  (CEQA) under Section 15319 (Annexations of Existing Facilities and Lots for
  Exempt Facilities) of the CEQA Guidelines. Annexations to a city or special district
  of areas containing existing facilities public or private structures developed to the
  density allowed by the current zoning or pre-zoning of either the gaining or losing
  governmental agency whichever is more restrictive, provided, however, that the
  extension of utility services to the existing facilities would a capacity to serve on
  the existing facilities.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-65:

  A RESOLUTION OF THE BOARD OF SUPERVISORS, AS THE GOVERNING
  BODY OF THE COUNTY OF LOS ANGELES, THE CONSOLIDATION FIRE
  PROTECTION DISTRICT OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY, THE LOS ANGELES
  COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT, THE CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF
  SAN GABRIEL, THE BOARD OF DIRECTORS OF THE COUNTY SANITATION
  DISTRICT NO. 15 OF LOS ANGELES COUNTY AND THE UPPER SAN
  GABRIEL VALLEY MUNICIPAL WATER DISTRICT, APPROVING AND
  ACCEPTING THE NEGOTIATED EXCHANGE OF PROPERTY TAX REVENUE
  RESULTING FROM THE ANNEXATION OF TERRITORY KNOWN AS
  ANNEXATION 2022-09 TO THE CITY OF SAN GABRIEL

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  7
   OTHER OPTIONS FOR CONSIDERATION
  The action of the City Council may be to approve; approve with modifications;
  or deny the Joint Tax Transfer application.

  If the City Council determines that the proposed application or any part of the
  application should be denied or modified, the appropriate motion should be
  adopted, including identifying any issues of concern with the Joint Tax Transfer
  Resolution, direct staff to modify the Resolution, and continue that the matter
  to the next regularly scheduled City Council meeting; or not adopt the Joint Tax
  Transfer Resolution, which would halt the Local Agency Formation Commission
  for the County of Los Angeles (LAFCO) process.

  J. APPROVAL OF CONTRACT WITH ECO SYSTEMS IN THE AMOUNT OF
  $66,500 PLUS A $13,300 CONTINGENCY FOR THE ROOFING PROJECT AT
  THE POLICE STATION [RESOLUTION NO. 24-56]

  The existing roof at Police Station hasn’t been replaced in over 20 years and is
  in urgent need of repairs due to a history of multiple leaks every year. Staff
  reached out to several local roofing companies for quotes and received
  responses from three with ECO Systems being the lowest responsive bidder.
  The total project cost is $66,500 plus a contingency of $13,300. A fiscal year
  2024-2025 General Fund appropriation increase in the amount of $79,800 is
  proposed to fund the project. Resolution No. 24-56 requests a General Fund
  appropriation increase of $79,800 to cover the required project budget for the
  roofing work at the Police Station. Special Project fund account 122-751-15-
  97-608 (Police Facility Roof Repair/Replacement) will be utilized to account for
  the project costs.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as re-roofing
  of existing roof at Police Station does not reasonably create a possibility that the
  work will have any significant affect to the environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a contract with ECO Systems in the amount of $66,500, plus a $13,300
  contingency, using account number 122-751-15-97-608 (Police Facility Roof
  Repair/Replacement). Additionally, staff recommends the City Council adopt
  Resolution No. 24-56 to increase General Fund appropriations in the amount
  of $79,800 for this project.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  8
   K. MEMORANDUM OF AGREEMENT WITH THE SAN GABRIEL VALLEY
  COUNCIL OF GOVERNMENTS FOR THE 2025 ACTIVE STREETS MISSION-
  TO-MISSION EVENT, TOTALING $15,000 WITH A MAXIMUM
  REIMBURSEMENT OF $10,000 [RESOLUTION NO. 24-57]

  On Sunday, June 22, 2025, from 3:00 P.M. to 8:00 P.M., the cities of San Gabriel,
  Alhambra and South Pasadena will be jointly hosting an open streets event,
  called 2025 Active Streets Mission-to-Mission. Each city is responsible for a
  proportional in-kind match or local fund match of the total event cost. San
  Gabriel’s required match is $15,000, which will likely be covered by the cost of
  staff attending planning meetings and staffing the event. The City will track
  expenses and staff time related to this event to satisfy the requirement. In
  addition to the $15,000 City contribution, up to $10,000 of related expenses
  beyond the $15,000 City’s share will be reimbursed to the City by the Metro
  grant administered through the SGVCOG. The attached Resolution No. 24-57
  requests an appropriation of $15,000 from the TDA local return fund to the
  special project fund, Account No. 124-800-44-96-603 (Mission-to-Mission
  Project), to cover the required $15,000 in-kind match.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: This item is not a
  Project as defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines, as due to its
  short duration, it has no potential for resulting in either a direct physical change
  in the environment, or a reasonably foreseeable indirect physical change in the
  environment.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  the final version of the Memorandum of Agreement between the San Gabriel
  Valley Council of Governments and the cities of San Gabriel, Alhambra, South
  Pasadena for the 2025 Active Streets Mission-to-Mission (Attachment A), once
  all three agencies mutually agree to the terms subject to the City Attorney’s
  approval. Additionally, staff recommends the City Council adopt Resolution No.
  24-57 to appropriate $15,000 from the Transportation Development Act local
  return fund to the special project fund, Account No. 124-800-44-96-603
  (Mission-to-Mission Project) for the above-mentioned event.

  L. PURCHASE OF NEW DRIVING UNDER  THE  INFLUENCE/DRUG
  RECOGNITION EXPERT VEHICLE - $59,924.04

  The Police Department is looking to purchase Driving Under the Influence/Drug
  Recognition Expert (DUI/DRE) equipment for this Fiscal Year (FY) 2024-2025.
  The vehicle will help the Police Department in DRE/DUI enforcement. This staff

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  9
   report is to request that City Council approve the amount of $59,924.04 to
  purchase a 2024 Chevrolet Silverado 1500 4WD Trail Boss utilizing funds from
  the Cannabis Tax Fund Grant as previously approved.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the purchase of one 2024
  Chevrolet Silverado 1500 4WD Trail Boss Vehicle from Sierra Chevrolet of
  Monrovia utilizing Cannabis Tax Fund Grant #17920 funds from account #124-
  751-57-99-383.

  M. 2023 STATE HOMELAND SECURITY PROGRAM GRANT ACCEPTANCE
  [RESOLUTION NO. 24-60]

  The City of San Gabriel has been awarded grant funds from the 2023 State
  Homeland Security Program for both the San Gabriel Police and Fire
  Departments in the amount of $90,000 and $1,300 respectively. Both are able
  to use these funds towards projects from the Department of Homeland Security
  Approved Equipment List and also to provide training. Budget adjustments to
  the Other Grants fund will be made to revenues and appropriations in the
  amount of $91,300. Funding for the purchases will be reimbursed through the
  State Homeland Security Program (SHSP) grant. Initial outlay would be $91,300,
  but would be full reimbursed, with no matching funds. There is no fiscal impact
  to the General Fund.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council adopt Resolution No. 24-60 to approve
  the following:

  Police Department
  1. Budget amendment to increase estimated revenue (account 186-3215) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants Fund by $90,000; and increase
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special
  Projects Funds (account 124-751-57-99-380) by $90,000.

  Fire Department

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  10
   2. Budget amendment to increase estimated revenue (account 186-2315) and
  appropriation (transfers out) in ‘Other Grants Fund by $1,300; and increase
  estimated revenue (transfers in) and appropriation in Capital/Special
  Projects Funds (account 124-761-57-99-380) by $1,300.

  3. Authorize both the Police Chief and Fire Chief to accept the State Homeland
  Security Program grant and purchase the items under the City’s purchasing
  policy.

  4. Authorize the City Manager to execute the subrecipient agreement between
  the City and the County of Los Angeles.

  N. APPROVAL OF A MEMORANDUM OF UNDERSTANDING WITH LAPD
  ACADEMY TO TRAIN POLICE RECRUITS AT A COST OF $3,000 PER RECRUIT

  The San Gabriel Police Department (SGPD) utilizes various police academies in
  Southern California to train San Gabriel Police Recruits. The San Gabriel Police
  Department is requesting the approval of a Memorandum of Understanding
  (MOU) between the Los Angeles Police Department’s Police Academy and the
  San Gabriel Police Department to meet its training needs. The SGPD Fiscal Year
  2024-2025 adopted budget includes funding for police academy tuition and
  related expenses utilizing account 121-751-00-45-033. The current tuition fees
  for the Los Angeles Police Department Police Academy are $3,000.00 per
  recruit. This cost is consistent with other police academy tuition fees.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve the Memorandum of
  Understanding between the Los Angeles Police Department Police Academy
  and the San Gabriel Police Department, which will allow San Gabriel Police
  Recruits to attend this academy on an as-needed basis and authorize the Police
  Chief to execute the agreement and any other necessary documents.

  O. THEATRE RENTAL FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY JEFFERSON MIDDLE SCHOOL

  Jefferson Middle School is planning a youth holiday concert to be held at the
  Mission Playhouse on December 12, 2024, with rehearsals on December 11, has
  requested a fee waiver. The event is free and open to the community. The
  school is requesting a waiver of the building rental fees of $1,100, the parking
  buyout fee of $2,550, and the building rental for rehearsal day, reducing their

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  11
   total fees from $13,848.55 to $9,486.55. The current rental subsidy account has
  sufficient funds to cover this amount.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council grant a waiver to Jefferson Middle
  School of the Playhouse building rental fee in the amount of $1,100 for the
  December 12, 2024, performance day.

  P. THEATRE RENTAL FEE WAIVER REQUEST BY OLYMPIA PHILHARMONIC
  SOCIETY

  Olympia Philharmonic Society is planning a youth orchestra concert at the
  Mission Playhouse on January 19, 2025, has requested a fee waiver. They are
  requesting that the total fee be reduced from $7,150.50 to $4,820.05. The event
  will be presented to the community at no charge for admission. The current
  rental subsidy account has sufficient funds to cover this amount.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council approve staff’s recommendation to
  grant a waiver of the San Gabriel Mission Playhouse rental fee in the amount of
  $2,330.00 for the January 19, 2025, performance day.

  Q. APPROVAL OF CONTRACT WITH ROOFING PLUS CONSTRUCTION INC. IN
  THE AMOUNT OF $28,750 PLUS A $6,000 CONTINGENCY FOR THE
  ROOFING REPAIR AT SMITH PARK POOL

  The existing roof at Smith Park Pool is more than 20 years old and is in need of
  roofing repairs due to severe leaking. The roof leaks in several areas and has
  affected the daily activity of the pool staff and users inside the building,
  especially during heavy rains. Public Works staff contacted professional roofing
  companies to obtain quotes for the roof repair. With the City Council’s approval
  staff aims to have the repair completed prior to the rainy season. Staff has
  requested approval from LA County Regional Park and Open Space District
  (RPOSD) to use the City’s allocation for this project. It is anticipated that RPOSD
  will approve the expenditure which will cover the project costs. In order to move

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  12
   forward with this project, staff is requesting an appropriation of $34,750 (repair
  costs plus contingency) from the General Fund to the special project fund,
  Account No. 122-850-15-97-608 to cover the required project budget for the
  roofing work at Smith Park Pool.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council authorize the City Manager to execute
  a contract with Roofing Plus Construction Inc. in the amount of $28,750 plus a
  contingency of $6,000 using Account Number 122-850-15-97-608 (Smith Park
  Pool Facility Roof Repair/Replacement). Additionally, staff recommends the City
  Council adopt Resolution No. 24-67 to appropriate $34,750 from the General
  Fund to Account Number 122-850-15-97-608 for the above-mentioned
  project.

  R. APPROVAL AND ACCEPTANCE OF DONATIONS TOTALING $7,500 FROM
  THE CALIFORNIA COMMUNITY FOUNDATION FUND AND THE ADOPTION
  OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-59 FOR A BUDGET INCREASE OF $7,500 FOR TWO
  PRODUCTIONS AT THE MISSION PLAYHOUSE

  San Gabriel Mission Playhouse staff are recommending that the City Council
  accept donations totaling $7,500 from the Friends of the Mission Playhouse
  account managed by the California Community Foundation (CCF) to offset
  costs of hosting two community productions. Staff have worked diligently with
  various third parties on a presentation of the Amanda Castro Band and a Will
  and Co production of A Christmas Carol. While staff anticipates offsetting most
  of the costs through ticketing, concessions and parking fees, additional funding
  is necessary to ensure these events do not rely on funding from the Mission
  Playhouse fund.

  Staff anticipates expenditures totaling $12,750 from the Mission Playhouse
  Special events account, 152-712-32-27-047. Revenue from ticket sales,
  concessions and parking is anticipates at $14,390 for the two proposed events.
  Additionally, donations from the Friends of the Mission Playhouse Donation
  fund as distributed by California Community Foundation totaling $7,500, this
  will offset the Mission Playhouse fund’s costs for the creation of thew new event
  offerings, if accepted by the City Council. Should the City Council accept the
  donations, an additional $7,500 will need to be appropriated to the Mission
  Playhouse Special Events account number 152-712-32-27-047 by adopting
  Resolution No. 24-59.

City Council Regular Meeting Agenda – November 19, 2024  13
   California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends the City Council accept the donation totaling $7,500 from
  California Community Foundation and adopt Resolution No. 24-59 to adjust
  the budget accordingly.

 5. PUBLIC HEARING – None.

 6. CONTINUED BUSINESS

  A. DISCUSSION REGARDING A FUTURE FARMERS’ MARKET

  In late April, the City and Supporting Arms launched the San Gabriel Farmers’
  Market. Despite many efforts, the Farmers’ Market was not able to consistently
  retain vendors, and attendance to the event decreased. At the August 20, 2024,
  City Council meeting, the City Council directed staff to return with an
  agreement to onboard Farm Habit as the new farmers market operator. The
  Council determined that the closure of Mission Drive adjacent to Blossom
  Market Food Hall would be the best location to relaunch the market and to host
  the market on Saturday mornings. At the September 17, 2024, City Council
  meeting, the Council continued the item to allow time for the owner of Farm
  Habit to attend the meeting. Prior to the scheduled October 15, 2024, City
  Council, staff received information from Farm Habit that resulted in removing
  the item from the agenda. The intent of this report is to request further direction
  from the City Council regarding the City’s approach for the farmers’ market.
  There is no fiscal impact related to this staff report.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends that the City Council discuss the matter related to farmers’
  market and direct staff to seek proposal from existing qualified market
  operators.

  ADJUSTMENTS AND APPROVAL OF RESOLUTION NO. 24-66 TO AMEND
  THE FISCAL YEAR 2024/25 BUDGET TO INCREASE EXPENDITURES BY
  $110,000 TO INCREASE VEHICLE SERVICE HOURS

  The City of San Gabriel operates an on-demand micro transit program, RideSG.
  The program allows residents and visitors alike to travel anywhere within the
  City of San Gabriel. Additional benefits are available through the RideSG Plus
  membership for residents 62 years of age and older and residents with a
  disability. Since the inception of the program staff have worked diligently to
  transition residents from the dial-a-ride service to RideSG and make
  incremental adjustments to the program to increase user satisfaction and
  service efficiency. However, given the unique and expansive service offered, the
  demand has now exceeded service capacity. Should the City Council approve
  the revisions to the service parameters and increase vehicle service hours, funds
  would need to be allocated from Proposition A to the RideSG expenditure
  account, 180-850-49-81-000 in the amount of $110,000 for fiscal year 2024/25.
  This would bring the total fiscal year 2024/25 allocation from $577,851 to
  $687,851. Annually, Proposition A expenditure costs will increase by $264,000
  per year, most likely increasing annually for the rising cost of labor. Every other
  year, the City exchanges Proposition A dollars for unrestricted General Fund
  dollars at an exchange rate of .75/1. Adding these additional costs will decrease
  the amount available of Proposition A funds available to exchange for General
  Fund dollars.

  California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA) Determination: Not a Project as
  defined in Section 15378 of the State CEQA Guidelines.

  Recommended Action:

  Staff recommends City Council:

  1. Approve the programmatic changes to the RideSG service, including
  reductions in the RideSG Plus service area;

  2. Adopt Resolution No. 24-66, authorizing the budget adjustment of
  $110,000 to cover the additional vehicle service hours from December 2024
  through April 2025; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager to execute the amended professional services
  agreement with Transdev, reflecting the updated fee schedule.
